summary:
plan.md is done; I checked the block ids but built and rendered nothing. Nan Shan: a sheer 64×64 tower with chamfered corners, white quartz fins every second block over gray glass and a warm gold slot in each face, topped by an open fin crown that peaks to y 381 and is lit white-gold, beside a three-box Breeze podium (two shifted gold-screen boxes under a dark-glass box) to y 46.
Sky Tower: a 55×56 tower with rounded corners and continuous white ribs over cyan glass, stepping in three times near the top to a glowing glass observatory with a stepped glass roof, a mast and a red light at y 397, on an 8-storey stone-and-glass podium with a lit lobby on Songgao Road.
It reads as these two buildings because the camera sees exactly what tells them apart: the fin crown and slotted faces of Nan Shan, the gold podium boxes, and the Sky Tower's white ribs and lit lantern top. Nan Shan: a sheer chamfered tower with quartz fins over gray glass, a split reveal and a lit open wheat-ear crown, on a gold-screened Breeze podium. Sky Tower: a ribbed white-and-cyan rounded shaft with a taper and a glowing observatory under a glass hip and a red-lit mast, on a glass-and-stone podium. Six parts; dusk lighting is scattered warm/cool windows, lit lobbies and crowns.

Nan Shan tower shell: Nan Shan tower shell built in parts/nanshan-shell.mjs. Shaft y19..352 has quartz fins every 2nd cell over gray/black glass, floor lines, four chamfered corners, and a 6-wide reveal slot on all four faces. Lobby base y4..17 is glass between quartz piers, with door bays on S, N and E and a y18 roof terrace with glass rail. make.sh finishes with no refused or off-palette writes.
polish: Roof slab y352, the crown above it and the aircraft lights are P2's; the reveal slots and fins here stop at y352, so the crown must carry the slots up to y381.
Lobby roof deck leaves air cells where (x-156)%6==3 and (z-6)%6==3 (z-6 for z); P6 must fill them with sea_lantern, plus planters and the planted ring around the shaft.
Lobby doors sit on the glass plane (z76, z7, x244). The canopies and the fascia over the doors are P6's.
mcd check lists 16 'unsupported' sea_lanterns at y17 just inside the lobby glass (e.g. 167,17,10). They sit under the solid y18 roof, so I took them as a false positive and did not chase it.
I did not run `mcd fit` or the full render sheet; I looked at one door-bay close-up only.

waste.what: Splitting each shaft face into two fin spans either side of the reveal slot, with trimmed chamfer ends and a matching floorLine call per span; also splitting lobby faces into segments around the door gaps
waste.cost: about 30 lines of coordinate and parity arithmetic, done by hand
waste.tool: finFace and lobbyGlass should take `skip` spans (slot and door gaps) and a `chamfer` inset, and floorLine should accept a list of y values

waste.what: Glazing the dx+dz=7 diagonal so the chamfer has no see-through gaps
waste.cost: a local loop over 4 corners × 334 rows
waste.tool: chamferCorner should fill the in-between diagonal glass cell itself

waste.what: doorBay is a single-plane door wall, so it needed a manual 16-wide gap, bay spacing, and glass fill above the transoms
waste.cost: 3 hand-placed bay rows plus glass fills
waste.tool: a `doorWall(g, span, face, bays)` helper that tiles bays across a span and glazes above them

companions.task: Detail the 45° chamfer faces and the door-bay transoms, and check the glass planes meet without see-through gaps
Fill the deck-light cells on the y18 lobby terrace and place the lit-window cells in the shaft glass

summary:
Breeze podium: Breeze podium built in parts/breeze-podium.mjs (62,198 blocks, 0 refused, 0 off-palette): P-A gold box with lit shopfronts (S/W/N), P-B gold box with N and S soffits, P-C dark-glass box with coping and mechanical box, terraces, café pergola, planters, kiosk P-K, link atrium L and covered walk W.
Plinth fills the ground gap under the street storey; the structure check shows no floating blocks from this part after the pergola fix.
Make.sh produces a whole build.nbt; plan.md checklist P3 ticked and seven elements.md items ticked; the fascia plaques and atrium/north-entry doors are not built.
polish: Fascia plaques (shop names) on the P-A y8 band over S/W/N shopfronts: not placed; the fascia band itself (smooth_quartz at depth 0..1, y8) is not laid, so plaqueFascia has no band to sit on.

Doors not cut: N main entry z16 x40..55 (16w x 4h glass under the P-B cantilever) and atrium doors z24/z59 x124..133. lobbyGlass and shopFront wrote glass there first, so the openings need a carve in the helper call.
P-A east face y4..8 is clear glass across x101 into the atrium; P-A roof coping 1 proud at y18 not added.
P-C deck is at y45 with coping y45..46 (plan says deck y46 with coping y46..47); mechanical box sits on y46..50 as specified.

Pergola: the beam-post at (99,34,21) hangs over a deck-light air cell at (99,33,21) (lights-grounds P6 cell); seven lattice trapdoors on the pergola rim are orphans (cosmetic). Atrium/P-A/P-B sea lanterns on the Nan Shan shell (x167..235, y17) are unsupported but belong to the shell part, not this one.
Deck and roof lights on the terraces are left air for P6 as the plan says; I did not place them.

waste.what: Ground plinth: each mass's plinth was worked out cell by cell (ground top from the GROUND map, fill from top+1 up to the floor) because no helper fills plinth from ground to floor.
waste.cost: one custom plinth() loop over ~6,000 footprint cells; one off-by-one (y < box.y0 vs <=) found only by the structure check
waste.tool: A build-library plinth(g, box) / groundTop-based fill helper that lays polished_andesite from the ground top to the floor under a footprint, and a note in plan.md that the street floor is y4 so the plinth ends at y3 inclusive.

waste.what: Air-only box fills for roof slabs, floors and soffit layers (STONE at y18, y19, y32, y33, y45) were hand-written loops with isAir checks.
waste.cost: about 8 fillAir calls; no retries after the first fix
waste.tool: A vocab helper floorSlab(g, box, y, block, {pick}) for an air-only layer of a box, with the per-cell pick (deck light grid) built in.

waste.what: Argument shapes were inconsistent across helpers: goldScreen and faceSpan take the [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1] array, while shopFront, terraceDeck and soffit take objects; the first build crashed on this.
waste.cost: one failed make run and an arr() wrapper
waste.tool: Normalise every helper to one box shape (object or array) and document it in the vocab header; the same mistake would hit every part.

waste.what: Pergola beams are not supported: the helper places beam slabs and lanterns inside the perimeter with no posts under them, so the whole roof group floats. I found it from the check output and added posts by hand.
waste.cost: one structure check, one extra loop of posts
waste.tool: pergola() should put a quartz post under every beam cell (or the beam grid must lie on the perimeter posts); a check in the helper would flag it.

waste.what: Fascia plaques: plaqueFascia needs a frame (at, face) that I could not work out without reading the source and a band that does not exist yet; I skipped the element.
waste.cost: about 2 minutes of reading; element not built
waste.tool: A fascia helper that lays the smooth_quartz fascia band at a given y across a shopFront and places the plaque in one call, so the frame is not needed.

waste.what: Footprint check (that each mass lies on # cells) was done by hand against the 6-block coarse map.
waste.cost: around 10 mass boxes checked mentally
waste.tool: mcd footprint <box> --plot 0 that tests a plot-local box against the coarse footprint and prints the ground tops under it.

waste.what: Visual check: I read one render (SE view) to judge the massing by eye.
waste.cost: one render, one image read
waste.tool: A tile per face with the gold screen and shop bays labelled, so a glance check is not needed for each face.

companions.task: Shop names on the P-A y8 fascia (S, W, N faces): the band layout and the plaque letters, so the fascia reads from the street.
The atrium and north-entry doors: cut the openings in the lobbyGlass wall and hang the door bays with transoms.
The plinth and ground-to-floor plinth course under each mass, including the west-edge drop at x0..11 z48..83, and the coping courses at y18, y32, and y45..46.
The pergola and terrace planters on the P-B north-east terrace: posts under every beam, planters on the deck.

summary:
Sky Tower shell: Sky Tower shell (plot 1) built in parts/sky-shell.mjs: podium z0..50 y0..41 with podiumFace facades, floor plates and roof slab; glass waist link z51..65 with roof terrace y30.
Tower shaft x1..55 z66..121 with r9 rounded corners, y15..343: white concrete ribs over cyan glass, light gray floor lines every 7, taper steps at y316/330/344 with smooth_quartz_slab ledge caps; lobby ring y1..14 with glass and smooth_quartz piers.
make.sh whole, 0 refused, 0 off-palette for this part; plan checklist P4 ticked; shaft, ribs and taper ticked in elements.md. Podium lobby, canopy and doors not built.
polish: Podium west (Songgao Rd) lobby: glass plane should be set back to x3 with doors z26..41 (doorBay) and the x0..2 canopy at y9..10 with sea_lantern underside, z18..50. Not built; the west face is a plain podiumFace at x0.
Waist link S-W: iron mullions every 3 not built, only corner iron; the terrace rail is glass_pane on the edges.
Tower lobby y1..14: doors on the S (z77 face, Sky lobby W x0..2 z84..103) and the W lobby doors are not cut; no interior lighting beyond sea_lantern on every 6th ring cell at y14.
Podium coping sticks out one cell at a few corners (check reports orphan polished_diorite at 292,41,2 and 310,41,17); those are podiumFace's proud coping and were left as is.
Shaft ring cyan glass and ribs are continuous; the observatory and crown (y344+) are parts 4 and 5, so the top of the shaft is open at y343.

waste.what: Per-cell loops over the rounded plan for the tower: outline sets, outer and second ring, parity ribs and floor lines, written with g.set one block at a time (about 130k sets).
waste.cost: About 15 minutes of design and roughly 130k set calls; the shaft was not written with a helper.
waste.tool: A single shape brush or helper for a rounded tapered shaft: roundedPlan(cx,cz,r,corner) plus ribFace per face, with taperStep applied at given rows and caps placed by the helper, not by hand.

waste.what: Footprint filter written by hand as a Proxy over the grid (onFp), because helpers do not check the footprint map and the part must build only on #.
waste.cost: One proxy, plus one debugging pass over a footprint that did not match the 3x3 map as I read it.
waste.tool: A build-library option such as guard(g, footprint) or a view like onFootprint(plot) that refuses writes outside the # cells, so each part gets it without writing its own filter.

waste.what: Air checks and state arguments were guessed for direct g.set calls (the library docs did not give the signature of set's state argument).
waste.cost: Two small corrections after reading placer() in vocab/h3.mjs.
waste.tool: A one-line note in the toolkit reference: g.set(x,y,z,block,state) takes a plain object for state, and an air-checked set (setAir) exists or does not.

waste.what: Checking the plan's footprint and ground by eye from the text maps (the 3x3 rows, the taper rows, the lobby ring).
waste.cost: Several minutes of counting rows.
waste.tool: mcd plan or a footprint-to-cell listing for the plot, printed with coordinates so a part can ask for the cells in a row or box.

waste.what: Running node with the toolkit path from a shell variable: zsh does not split an unquoted $MCD, so the first check failed.
waste.cost: One failed command.
waste.tool: Document in the brief that zsh needs the mcd path written out, or ship a wrapper script on the PATH.

companions.task: The lobby and waist-link glazing: mullion spacing every 3 on the waist link, the podium west lobby glass set back to x3 with its doors, and the lit lobby ceiling strip.
The lobby doors and the entrance approach from Songgao Road: the slab-ramp approach from the street to the W doors, with a landing and no stairs.
Light the lobby ring and the ledge caps at the taper steps so the tower reads lit at dusk, and check that roofs and terraces give no mob spawns.
The podium roof slab at y40 and the coping ring, checking the proud corner pieces that show as orphans in the structure check.

summary:
Nan Shan crown: Nan Shan crown (P2) built in parts/nanshan-crown.mjs: roof slab y352 (air cells only), hollow plant box, wheat-ear fin crown y353..381 with reveal edge fins and chamfer posts, froglight glow, four red aircraft lights at y382.
make.sh runs whole; this part shows 9517 placed, no REFUSED writes, no OFF-PALETTE; fit OK; check reports 0 floating blocks after the slab/plant-box fix.
Plan.md checklist P2 ticked, elements.md crown items ticked, P2 note added to plan.md Notes. Zoom renders from south and east read as fins peaking to the reveal with the red lights on its edges; the hero view was not rendered.
polish: Structure check still lists orphans from this part: the pearlescent froglights at y353 and the red glass of the aircraft lights touch the build on one face only (about 8 of the 14 orphans). These are deliberate light placements; the lights part may want to back them.
Aircraft-light red glass sits at z11 and z76, one cell outside the tower footprint (the plan lists these cells), and the cells at x196 and x199 have no fin under them, so they hang from the lamp.
Reveal slot is open in the crown only: the plan's 3-deep slot side walls (z12..15 / z72..75) are not built here; the shell owns the slot in the shaft.
Plan's even-offset fin rule collides with the reveal edge fins at x195/x200 (odd/even parity), so I added a fin at x194 for the aircraft lamp; the plan's fin rhythm is off by one at the reveal.
Chamfer posts are single cells on dx+dz=6 at top y366 with no glazing; the plan's sawtooth glass is not built in the crown (it is the shell's job in the shaft).
Plant box is hollow (walls, moss floor, azalea/leaves at y354), not the solid gray_concrete volume the elements list reads as; a tidy visual but a judgement call.
Lobby sea lanterns at y17 are reported UNSUPPORTED by check; they belong to the shell/lights parts, not this one.
The hero dusk view from the Elephant Mountain trail was not rendered; only south and east zooms were checked.

waste.what: Worked out the crown fin positions and tops by hand: even offsets, the chamfer cut, the reveal edges, and top = 381 − dist/2 clamped to 366 for every face.
waste.cost: about 40 fin cells computed in my head across four faces, plus the chamfer diagonals; one mistaken parity had to be fixed after the first build.
waste.tool: a crownFaces(box, reveal, {topCentre, topMin, step}) helper in vocab/h2 that returns the fin list per face with tops, so the parity, chamfer and reveal rules live in one place.

waste.what: Printed the y352 layer by hand with a throwaway script to find who owned each cell, and mixed up plot-local and grid coordinates (grid = plot + MARGIN 2), which sent me down a wrong path about the shell's slab.
waste.cost: two build cycles, one wrong edit (roof slab removed then restored), about 6 minutes.
waste.tool: mcd layer build.nbt --y 352 --box x0,z0,x1,z1 printing PLOT-LOCAL coordinates and owner part per cell (from runParts) would have shown the shell/crown split at once.

waste.what: Refused writes on the shell's perimeter course at y352 were only visible in the REFUSED log; I had to infer which cells the shell owned.
waste.cost: 376 refused writes, fixed by checking blockAt before laying each cell.
waste.tool: runParts could list refused cells as a box per part, or a helper like layAir(g, box, block) that skips non-air cells silently by design.

waste.what: Chamfer diagonal fins were placed through crownFin on a one-cell degenerate box to reuse its logic.
waste.cost: 20 posts, one line of trickery.
waste.tool: a post(g, [x,y,z], {top, cap}) helper in the crown vocab for a single fin cell that is not on a face.

waste.what: Ticked plan.md and elements.md by hand after reading the live checklist, because other workers edit the same file.
waste.cost: 5 Edit calls and two re-reads.
waste.tool: mcd plan tick P2 --elements items-of P2, which marks checklist and element lines together and re-reads the file atomically.

companions.task: Set the 64-block fin frame and the 4 aircraft-light masts at y352..382, the high-level work that needs a rig rather than a ladder, and check each fin top against the 381/366 profile before the lamps go on.
Place and aim the white-gold froglight glow inside the crown (pearlescent at the crown floor, ochre every third fin) and check the crown's floor cells for light so no spawn cell is dark.
Plant the hollow plant box at y353..364 (moss floor, azaleas, persistent leaves) so it reads as a planted roof garden through the fins.
Fit the red glass hoods of the aircraft lights and the reveal slot's glass back wall (the shell's job in the shaft, but the crown's opening should match).

summary:
Sky Tower crown: Sky Tower crown built in parts/sky-crown.mjs: observatory y344..371 with rib cage to y376, stepped glass hip y372..384 (plus a y372 glass bridge ring), mast y385..396 and the red aircraft light y397..398. make.sh ran to a whole build.nbt; the part report shows 28554 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette.
The east zoom reads as a stepped glass pyramid with iron ribs, a mast and a red top light. The south zoom shows the observatory rib cage.
Plan.md's P5 tick and the Notes line are added, and the four elements.md P5 items are ticked.
polish: Crown is FLOATING in `mcd check` only because the Sky Tower shell (P4) is still a stub in this copy; it rests on the shell's y343 taper top and should connect once P4 merges. Re-run check after the merge.
No lights are placed on the glass hip or the mast; lights-grounds (P6) should cover the roof light so no mob spawns on the stepped hip.
Full-site `mcd render --front n --tiles` was not run (the whole 313x401x131 build is slow); I checked with two `mcd zoom` views (south at the observatory, east at the hip and mast) instead.
The observatory's roof is a mostly-air interior under the glass hip (only the ring and lights sit at y371). Checked by eye that it reads as a lit lantern, but not in the lit-level pass (`mcd light`).

waste.what: Worked out plot-local to site coordinates by hand (x + 252 for plot 1) to aim the zoom views at the crown.
waste.cost: 2-3 coordinate calculations and two zoom retries
waste.tool: A `mcd zoom --plot 1 --at x,y,z` option (or a plot-local flag) so the plan's coordinates pass through unchanged.

waste.what: Found by eye that the glass hip's first course (x6..50) sits 2 cells off the rib cage and would float, then wrote a bridge ring by hand.
waste.cost: One extra helper loop and one check run
waste.tool: A glassHip/observatory option that joins its first course to the surrounding ring (e.g. a `joinRing` flag), or a note in plan.md that the observatory ceiling is solid at its outer ring.

waste.what: Checked floating and support with `mcd check` on the whole site, where most of the output belongs to other parts (Nan Shan shell's lantern supports), so I had to filter it by hand to find my own findings.
waste.cost: One long check read
waste.tool: `mcd check --part <name>` or a per-part filter on the STRUCTURE report, so each worker sees only its own floating groups.

companions.task: Check the stepped glass hip's joins to the rib cage and the glass ring at y372, so the roof reads as one sealed glass plane and not a floating stack of courses.
Light the observatory's lantern ceiling and the hip top (the lights-and-grounds part), so the crown reads warm at dusk and no roof is left dark.
Confirm the red aircraft light's lamp, red glass housing and the mast's rod rest at y396 and y397, so the light is seen from the Elephant Mountain trail at 200 blocks up.

summary:
Lights and grounds: P6 lights and grounds built in parts/lights-grounds.mjs: T-N/T-S porte-cochère canopies (8 quartz piers, lanterns), lit windows on both towers (S/E densest), decks and planters on the P-A/P-B/P-C/T-L/S-P/S-W roofs with sea_lantern grids, the west slab ramp, and two Breeze fascia plaques.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt: this part placed 14938 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette; fit OK, unknownBlocks empty.
Street lamp posts are not built; the part is not ticked in plan.md's checklist for that reason.
polish: Street lamp posts (fence post + lantern) not built: the plaza ground inside the plot sits outside the footprint, so there is no free ground for them yet; the plan's gate and path lamps need the P3 podium's street edge first.

Roof decks (P-A y19, P-B y33, P-C y46, S-P y41, S-W y31, T-L y18) and planters float in the standalone build because the P3 podium and P4 sky-shell roofs are still stubs; they should sit on the roofs once the parts merge. Check again after merge.
Shopfront lights, the café pergola lanterns and the atrium roof lights belong to P3 and are not built here; plan.md elements 'podium lit shopfronts' is only half done.

Fit/check flag the lobby sea_lanterns at y17 as unsupported (nothing below to hang from). They are the P1 shell's ceiling lights and are capped by the y18 roof, so this looks like a checker false positive; not changed here.
The two Breeze fascia plaques (BREEZE, NAN SHAN) were placed on the south face at y7 by the helper's frame, but only the zoom of the canopy was viewed; the plaque orientation was not checked by eye.

plan.md's checklist still has [ ] P6, and elements.md ticks cover only the canopies, the lit windows and the ramp; the deck and planter items were built but left unticked because their P3 halves are missing.

waste.what: Drew each roof deck as a hand-picked rectangle inside the mass boxes and the footprint rows, and worked out the plot 1 footprint rows by counting the ASCII map.
waste.cost: about 10 rectangle boxes computed by hand, plus two rounds of footprint counting
waste.tool: A footprint-mask deck helper, e.g. terraceMask(g, plot, y, {under the footprint and clear of a shaft box}), which lays deck and rails from the footprint map and the mass's extent.

waste.what: Wrote my own terrace() instead of vocab terraceDeck, because terraceDeck lays bottom slabs and a glass_pane rail on one leaves half a block of air (fit flagged 1361 issues).
waste.cost: one full rewrite and one rebuild (about 2 min)
waste.tool: A deck option on terraceDeck for full blocks (deck: 'smooth_stone' with no slab type), or a fit rule that accepts rails over bottom slabs in deck heights.

waste.what: Found by inspection that litWindows sits in the box's face plane, so lights stuck out between fins (orphans). Had to re-box every call to the glass plane.
waste.cost: one rebuild and one check pass (about 3 min)
waste.tool: litWindows documentation saying the box face is the plane itself, or an option for the glass-plane offset (e.g. {inset: 1}).

waste.what: Read the shell's lobby deck-light grid by hand to match its origin (x 156 + 6k + 3, not the strip's x0).
waste.cost: one check of the block grid by read-back
waste.tool: A shared lightGrid origin constant in base.mjs, so each part uses the same offset for the same mass.

waste.what: Checked the block under each lantern by reading the NBT (g.get) and did the zoom of the canopy by eye.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls
waste.tool: mcd check --explain <x,y,z> printing the support chain for a flagged block.

companions.task: Design and place the street lamp posts (fence post plus hanging lantern) along the Songren Road and plaza edges, every 8-10 blocks, with lantern spots checked against the light map.
Check that the terrace decks and rail coping meet the podium parapets on the merged roofs (P-A, P-B, P-C, S-P), so no deck is left floating after merge.
Light the shopfront interiors behind the Breeze colonnade (warm strip, shop windows) and the lobby glazing, so the street storey reads lit at dusk.

summary:
inspection: Fit is now clean (2710 issues → 0): the 1888 floating shutters and 822 glass rails on bottom slabs are fixed.
Shutters: vocab/h3.mjs goldScreen puts yellow_terracotta behind each lattice trapdoor instead of glass.
Rails: breeze-podium.mjs no longer lays its bottom-slab terraceDeck decks; lights-grounds.mjs lays the full-block deck and its rails.
WALK still ok (start 1, reachedCells 5748, no rooms listed); ./make.sh rebuilt build.nbt, and both checks were run after the rebuild.

waste.what: Worked out which module placed each flagged cell. The fit output shows only about 14 sample lines of 2710 issues, with no cause grouping, and its coordinates are grid coordinates (MARGIN 2 offset), not plot-local. I converted by hand (grid x/z minus 2) and traced the flagged rails to two parts that both lay the same terrace.
waste.cost: about 6 tool calls: reading breeze-podium, lights-grounds, and goldScreen source, plus one fit run to see the sample
waste.tool: fit should group issues by cause (helper name, e.g. goldScreen south face / terraceDeck rails) with the owning part and plot-local coordinates. It should also say whether a part lays a block that a later part already lays over.

waste.what: Had to read the goldScreen helper to see that the trapdoor's backing was the glass plane, to choose the fix.
waste.cost: 1 read of vocab/h3.mjs and one edit
waste.tool: fit message could name the helper and the backing it wants, e.g. 'shutter's wall is glass: a solid backing is needed'.
